gaps.sentence: The new bridge ___ (open) by the mayor next month.
gaps.explanation: Future simple passive: will be + opened, with the agent in a by-phrase.

gaps.sentence: The manuscript is too fragile ___ (handle) without gloves.
gaps.explanation: Passive to-infinitive: to be + past participle. The manuscript receives the handling.

gaps.sentence: Several issues remain ___ (resolve) before the launch.
gaps.explanation: 'Remain' + passive infinitive (to be resolved) expresses unfinished business.

gaps.sentence: While the sets ___ (build), the actors rehearsed in a warehouse.
gaps.hint: two past actions, one passive and ongoing
gaps.explanation: Past continuous passive (were being built) for the longer background action.

gaps.sentence: The theatre ___ in 1897 and reopened last year.
gaps.explanation: A finished date (1897) takes past simple passive: was + built.

gaps.sentence: The match ___ (abandon) because of the storm, so we got a refund.
gaps.explanation: Modal passive with have to: had to be + past participle for past obligation.

gaps.sentence: The bridge ___ (inspect) twice a year for signs of corrosion.
gaps.explanation: 'Twice a year' marks a routine: present simple passive, is + inspected.

gaps.sentence: I couldn't use the meeting room because it ___ (clean) all morning.
gaps.explanation: Past continuous passive: was being + cleaned over a period in the past.
